page: Microsoft Azure HB368-192rs_v5 is a high-performance compute instance from the HBv5 server family, designed for demanding computational workloads. Powered by dedicated Intel processors with an x86_64 architecture, this server provides 192 dedicated virtual CPUs. It features 448.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.33 GB per core. The instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, ensuring robust virtualization and resource isolation.

For storage-intensive operations, the server is equipped with 15,851 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Azure Premium Storage. It is also RDMA-capable, enabling low-latency, high-throughput inter-node communication for clustered environments. The hardware profile lacks integrated GPUs, focusing its resource allocation entirely on high-density CPU execution and massive local storage capacity.

This hardware configuration represents a highly specialized, resource-dense class. The combination of dedicated high-core-count compute, substantial local NVMe storage, and RDMA networking makes it highly cost-efficient for large-scale parallel processing where external network bottlenecks must be minimized. Appropriate workloads include high-performance computing, large-scale simulations, clustered database systems, and intensive data-processing pipelines.
